title: Depth of a finite module over a Noetherian local ring via Ext from the residue field
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], i.e. a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, and let $M$ be a nonzero finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For $i\ge0$ let $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,M)$ be the $i$-th Ext group of [def-pc-ext] in the abelian category of $R$-modules. Then there is an integer $i\ge0$ with $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,M)\neq0$, and the depth $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ of [def-weil-pbc-depth] is finite and equals the smallest integer $i\ge0$ such that $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(\kappa,M)\neq0$.

proof.text: Nakayama gives mM != M. Thus depth is the supremum of lengths of M-regular sequences in m. The support-dimension bound, Module.supportDim_le_ringKrullDim, and finite local Krull dimension make this supremum a finite natural number d. The empty regular sequence makes the set nonempty, so ENat.sSup_mem_of_nonempty_of_lt_top supplies an M-regular sequence rs of length d in m.

Let L = ULift M and K = ULift (R/m) in the common universe max u v of the original statement. ULift.moduleEquiv identifies L with M and K with R/m; LinearEquiv.isRegular_congr preserves regularity and LinearEquiv.support_eq preserves support. Module.support_eq_zeroLocus and Ideal.annihilator_quotient give Supp(K) = V(m). Nakayama gives mL != L. These are exactly the hypotheses of the two Rees implications in Mathlib.RingTheory.Depth.Rees.

Transport rs to L and apply ModuleCat.subsingleton_ext_of_exists_isRegular, the regular-sequence-to-Ext implication of Rees, with ideal m and first argument K. It gives Subsingleton (Ext K L j) for every j < d.

If Ext K L d were subsingleton, the preceding vanishing and the elementary dichotomy j < d or j = d for j < d+1 give vanishing in every degree below d+1. Apply ModuleCat.exists_isRegular_of_exists_subsingleton_ext, the other Rees implication, using Supp(K) = V(m), to obtain an L-regular sequence of length d+1 in m. Transport it back to M. Its length is bounded by the supremum defining depth, so d+1 <= d, a contradiction. By not_subsingleton_iff_nontrivial the degree-d Ext group is nontrivial. The same proof covers d=0 without a separate base case.

mathlib_candidate.how: Rees' theorem (read by sed -n 130,175p): for R Noetherian, M finite with IM < M and n : ℕ, Ext^i(R/I, M) = 0 for all i < n iff there is an M-regular sequence of length n in I. With I = m this gives: depth(M) ≥ n iff Ext^i(κ,M) = 0 for i < n, once one adds (a) Nakayama (mM ≠ M for M nonzero finite over a local ring), (b) the agreement of Mathlib's RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular with the regular sequences of [def-weil-pbc-depth] and that a regular sequence of length ≥ n has an initial piece of length n which is regular, (c) Shrink (R ⧸ I) ≅ R/I and Mathlib's Ext against [def-pc-ext], and (d) finiteness of depth(M) (Stacks 00LR/00LK) for the existence of a nonzero Ext. Several lines, not one: candidate, not a leaf (B8). Upstream Mathlib (not pinned) has IsLocalRing.depth_eq_sSup_length_isRegular in RingTheory/Depth/Basic.lean.
